title: Confused calibration follow up
body:
This is a follow-up to #770 
Please provide an option to send an ad hoc calibration to a G6 no matter what the current sensor state.
The G6 when started with a code has a very big signal error (usually 2-4 mmol too high). This can be calibrated back in range but if you get a confused calibration during this process then the sensor will stop giving data. There is (currently) a brief window when you can send a new calibration to fix the confused state but if you miss this the sensor stays crashed. 
By default xDrip turns off the calibration menu item after a few minutes of "confusion".
If there was an emergency way to give a calibration then the sensor could be recovered without having to do a stop/start (wait 2 hours) and then try the calibration sequence again.

Having an emergency calibration option would also resolve issue #1234

I never found any solution to this myself. after dumping about 300$ in sensors. In my experience or from what I tried. there was 0 work around. I attempted todo the standard Dexcom solutions when fail calibrations occur: waiting 2 hours & retry. No luck at all. No longer can use xDrip because of its flaws with the G6 I encountered

I have been using G6 for more than a year now.  My first two transmitter were 81XXXX.  The next two were 8JXXXX and 8QXXXX.
I have never needed to calibrate on a new sensor.
I do calibrate every time I restart.  I have never used a single G6 sensor for just 10 days.
I have provided detail instructions for doing all that in the facebook group:
https://www.facebook.com/groups/xDripG5

I always use initial calibration for calibrating, after having disabled double calibration.  Again, all the details are provided in the instructions.

Never calibrate when the trend is not flat or at least very close to flat.
https://navid200.github.io/xDrip/docs/Calibration.html

How to calibrate a G6:
https://navid200.github.io/xDrip/docs/Calibrate-G6.html
